judged_text: The credentialId-less destination branch calls createEvent(c, event) without destination.externalId (line ~377) while the reference writer now stores `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`, which is undefined on that branch — the old code stored evt.destinationCalendar.externalId. Bookings created through the credentialId-less destination branch get calendar references with externalCalendarId undefined, so their later update/delete falls into the GoogleCalendarService fallback that this same diff broke (undefined calendarId) — those Google events can never be moved or cancelled.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `event.destinationCalendar` entries without `destination.credentialId`, it calls `createEvent(c, event)` (no third arg) inside `destinationCalendarCredentials.map(...)`. But `CalendarManager.createEvent` was changed to return `externalId` from the optional third parameter, and `EventManager` now writes calendar references using `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` (replacing the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). Therefore, events created via the credentialId-less branch will produce `EventResult.externalId === undefined`, causing stored calendar references to have `externalCalendarId` undefined. This is a correctness regression directly shown by the diff and can break later update/delete routing that depends on `externalCalendarId`.
